items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: But Don thought that I could do it, and thank God he let me try.

ctx.x: And that was good for a while. And pretty soon we started getting different bookings, and we’d get ourselves a group, a rhythm section, and yeah, we’re on the road.

On the road again. But I think the next major thing that happened was then we went to Vegas to visit a friend of ours who lived there. And we were on our way to Chicago to work at Mr. Kelly’s in Chicago. And so we had the kids in the car and everything, and we went to Las Vegas to visit this friend, and we saw him, we stayed a few days, and one day we bumped into this guy on the street, who used to be Charlie Ventura’s manager, Don Palmer. And Don Palmer says, “what are you doing here?” And we said we’re just on…
maybe you’ll get something through them hearing you, you know, maybe you’ll get a contract to come back or something.” So we said well— he sai, “I’ll get you a bass player and drummer.”
